label: septate-nodulose
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being partitioned internally by transverse septa that show on the surface as small nodules or cross-ridges. NOTE: Usual in Juncus, Cyperaceae and Poaceae leaves and culms; PATO has no septate quality.
reason: A standard character of leaf blades and sheaths in graminoids (cross-partitions felt as nodules). Neither PATO nor FLOPO has a septate or partitioned quality.
A raceme shortened so that it looks like an umbel. FLOPO:0991031 umbelliform already lists 'umbellate-racemose' as a related synonym.
Sphagnum cortical and hyaline cells 'aporose' = without pores. PATO:0001821 imperforate means having no opening.
Lower bracts that look like leaflets are foliaceous, and the previous review mapped foliaceous to PATO:0002457 leaf-like. A leaflet is a leaf part, so the difference is too small to need a term.
A forb is a non-graminoid herb, a growth form of the whole plant. The herbaceous part is PATO:0002352; 'not grass-like' has no term and is lost.

label: latiseptate
definition: A flattened quality inhering in a fruit by virtue of its being compressed parallel to the septum, so that the septum lies across the broadest diameter of the fruit. NOTE: Brassicaceae silicles; the opposite is angustiseptate (compressed at right angles to the septum). Sibling of FLOPO:0991103 depressed.
reason: A precise and widely used fruit character in Brassicaceae. PATO's flattened terms are tied to animal body axes, not to the septum.
Ringlike discs, scars and nectaries are ring-shaped. PATO:0002539 has the exact synonyms ring-shaped and annular.
Caliculate = bearing a calyculus (an outer series of small bracts below the involucre or calyx). PO:0009063 epicalyx has calyculus as a synonym.

target: docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md (head-shaped FLOPO:0991097 for stigma and stylehead; capitate FLOPO:0991006 for inflorescence and cyme)
reason: 'Sub-' is the approximate-value cue ('suborbicular'). The value is head-shaped for a stigma and capitate for an inflorescence, as the two FLOPO classes divide them.

target: new: quality of the indumentum elements (scaly PATO_0001804 on the bearer + trichome PO_0000282 appressed FLOPO:0991064)
reason: Lepidote is scaly (previous rule C235), and 'appressed' describes the scales, not the leaf. One record for the bearer and one for its scales keeps both without a compound term.
Sphagnum hyaline cells without fibrils (the thickening bands of the cell wall) = not fibrillary. PATO:0002134 is defined as containing fibrils.

target: new: quality of the indumentum elements (hairy PATO_0000454 on the bearer + trichome PO_0000282 black PATO_0000317)
reason: A colour of the hairs joined to 'hairy'. The colour belongs to the hairs (part of the part), so it needs no term for each colour.
'Sub-' + chartaceous; chartaceous is a synonym of PATO:0104010 papyraceous. The value is papyraceous with value_qualifier 'sub'.

label: pseudopeltate
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being attached just inside its basal margin, with the basal lobes overlapping so that it appears peltate. NOTE: Fern rhizome scales; sibling of FLOPO:0991107 peltate.
reason: A distinct fern scale character set against peltate ('pseudopeltate or peltate'), so it is not the approximate-value pattern.
Summer-green plants carry green leaves only in the growing season and lose them in winter. That is the plant-level deciduous quality, the opposite of PATO:0001733 evergreen (plant).
French cannelé = fluted (trunk, stem, petiole). The previous rule C197 maps fluted to PATO:0001948 furrowed.
Rugate perispores and sheaths have wrinkles or elongated low ridges, which is PATO:0001359 rugose (many wrinkles or creases).

label: glandular-scaly
definition: A scaly quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with scales that are glands (peltate glandular trichomes). NOTE: Child of PATO:0001804 scaly; same model as FLOPO:0991173 glandular-pubescent.
reason: A recurrent indumentum type (Rhododendron, Lamiaceae, Myricaceae) that the previous review would treat like glandular-pubescent. Gland-dotted is about dots in the tissue, not scales.
A cyme with a flat-topped, corymb-like outline. The shape is PATO:0002455; the cymose branching has no term and is not kept.

target: rachilla extension absent (needs a FLOPO part class: rachilla extension, part of spikelet rachilla PO_0009080)
reason: A standard grass character: the rachilla does not go on beyond the uppermost floret. It is the absence of the extension, not of the rachilla, and PO has no class for the extension.

target: new: quality of the indumentum elements (puberulous FLOPO:0991049 on the bearer + trichome PO_0000282 falciform PATO_0002215)
reason: Puberulent with minute hooked hairs. Puberulous is FLOPO:0991049, and the hook belongs to the hairs (PATO:0002215 has the synonyms uncinate and hooked).
Explanate = spread out flat (labellum, stigmas, corolla). This follows rule C228 (plane = flat).

label: apomictic
definition: A reproductive quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its producing seeds, or in ferns sporophytes, without fertilization, so that its offspring are genetically identical to it. NOTE: Probably at the edge of PATO's scope (a mode of reproduction); includes fern apogamy.
reason: A real and often stated reproductive quality of the whole plant (Taraxacum, Rubus, Cyrtomium). Neither PATO nor FLOPO has a term for asexual seed or sporophyte formation.

target: new: quality of the indumentum elements (scaly PATO_0001804 on the bearer + trichome PO_0000282 punctiform PATO_0001366)
reason: Covered with minute scales that look like dots (Bromeliaceae). This is scaly, and the dot-like look belongs to the scales.
A margin with minute teeth tipped by small calluses. The toothed margin is PATO:0001205; the callose tips have no term and are not kept.
Floppy leaves and pedicels are limp, the opposite of rigid. Rigid maps to PATO:0001545 inflexible (C186), so floppy is PATO:0001544 flexible.
The dots are resin glands on or in the tissue, which is what FLOPO:0991174 gland-dotted defines.

label: obtrapeziform
definition: A trapezoid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being trapezoid with the longer of the two parallel sides at the apex, away from the point of attachment. NOTE: Same model as FLOPO:0991185 obtriangular.
reason: PATO:0002044 trapezoid has no orientation. The previous review added obtriangular for the same kind of inverted shape.

label: pseudomonoicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte by virtue of its male gametoecia being borne on dwarf male plants that grow on the leaves or stems of the female plants. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991093 autoicous.
reason: A standard sexual condition in moss floras that is distinct from autoicous and dioicous. No term exists for it.
Neutral ray or basal flowers have neither working stamens nor working carpels, so they are sterile. The rule is limited to flowers (the earlier rejection of 'sterile' was as a part name).
